column1: # PB-TOK-1: the JOIN between the ONE machine-readable token source and the Android theme.
# internal/design/tokens.json is the single origin. This table says which token each
# <color name=...> in app/src/main/res/values/colors.xml IS, and android/gate/s16_tokens_test.go
# checks the values actually agree -- in BOTH directions, so a colour resource with no row here
# is a value that entered the theme without passing through the origin.
# WHY A TABLE AND NOT A NAMING CONVENTION. A convention is a mapping nobody can review, and the
# two names differ on purpose: the token names are the design source's CSS custom properties
# (--p-bg) and the resource names are Android's (swarm_background). This is the arrangement
# android/connectivity-policy.tsv and android/fcm-priority.tsv already use, and for the same
# reason S13 gave: one artifact both a Go gate and a Kotlin test read.
# PB-TOK-5 (S22a): ALL SIXTEEN COLOURS, not three. The join was correct and under-fed -- it ran
# --p-bg, --p-ink and --p-ink2 through a fence built for the whole palette, so thirteen colours
# stayed pinned against a design source no screen could consume, and the fence was green the
# entire time because there was nothing on the other side to disagree with.
# PB-TOK-6 (S22a): THE KIND COLUMN. The gate used to sniff the value -- anything starting with #
# was a colour, everything else had "no ARGB form" and was refused. That is wrong about
# --p-tabbg (rgba(8,9,10,0.88) IS a colour), cannot tell --p-grain (0.05) from --p-display-wt
# (650), and has no expectation to violate when a token changes kind. The kind here must equal
# the kind internal/design/tokens.json declares; the origin is upstream and wins. A kind with no
# converter in the gate FAILS rather than being skipped, which is what stops the other fifteen
# tokens from being permanently unshippable.
# The five `dimen` tokens (--p-card-r, --p-sheet-r, --p-btn-r, --p-chip-r, --p-dot-r) belong in
# this table too, against values/dimens.xml. They are PB-DS's to add with that file; the gate
# already carries their converter and will scan dimens.xml the moment it exists.
# Columns: token <TAB> android_resource <TAB> kind <TAB> note
#token
--p-bg
column4: The window background. This is the value that was wrong: colors.xml declared #FF101114 against the origin's #08090a and called it a placeholder.

column1: --p-card
column4: Card fill: session row, filter chip, agent message bubble, tool card.

column1: --p-elev
column4: One ladder step up from card, and the only step there is. Substrate bans drop shadows, so elevation is expressed as a lighter surface (ADR-007 B134 decision 4).

column1: --p-well
column4: Recessed: the command well in the approval sheet, and the terminal peek's ground.

column1: --p-hair
column4: Every 1px border, the tab bar's top rule, the tool card's header divider.

column1: --p-ink
column4: Primary text. Also previously divergent (#FFE6E8EB against #f7f8f8).

column1: --p-ink2
column4: Secondary text: labels, timestamps, the need summary under a session row.

column1: --p-ink3
column4: Tertiary: section labels, agent name, sheet context line, inactive tab. Also the Completed group (PB-TOK-8) and, per inventory G2, the offline machine dot.

column1: --p-hero
column4: Brand and live: the LIVE counter, selected chip, active tab, user message bubble, terminal peek foreground.

column1: --p-hero-ink
column4: Ink on hero fills. Near-black green, not a neutral.

column1: --p-att
column4: Attention. Bound to status.Group NeedsInput (PB-TOK-8) and to the expiry countdown.

column1: --p-work
column4: Bound to status.Group Working (PB-TOK-8). Also the workbar gradient's opaque stop.

column1: --p-ok
column4: Bound to status.Group ReadyForReview (PB-TOK-8, ADR-007 B134 decision 1 -- green moves to review, NOT to done). Also diff additions and the chip presence dot.

column1: --p-err
column4: Error and deny. Also diff deletions and the composer's stop button.

column1: --p-cta-bg
column4: CTA fill. Value-aliases --p-hero TODAY and keeps its own row and its own resource on purpose: a future skin can break the alias, and a join that deduplicated by value would not notice it had.

column1: --p-cta-ink
column4: CTA ink. Value-aliases --p-hero-ink, same reasoning as the row above.

column1: --p-tabbg
column4: The tab bar's translucent fill. Typed `effect` until 2026-08-01 because it is paired with a backdrop blur -- but the blur is the effect and this is the FILL, and an audit committee found the miscategorisation was what made the "all 16 colours reach the app" claim true. rgba(8,9,10,0.88) -> #E008090A.
